answer: Sybil resistance comes from stake-weighted identity: each agent must lock a bond proportional to its claimed influence, and votes are weighted by that bond. To register, an agent also completes a unique proof-of-personhood voyage verified by peers. Forging thousands of identities then becomes a hollow strategy, since each fake node demands real capital and attestation. The atlas of trust is thus built on costly, verifiable commitments rather than free accounts, making mass identity creation economically irrational for adversaries.
